svg.title: This is an explicit standard-quantum intervention discriminator between two sources with identical passive words. It is not a test separating Shadow Theory from ordinary quantum mechanics. It tests the admitted physical source models after expanding the readout catalogue. No history needs to be discarded: retain all first two symbols and the probe outcome, and use the joint event “second symbol zero and click”. Its unconditional probability is zero in the parent and 800/91809 in the new source. A controller may schedule the same fixed probe after two ticks; selection of the joint event is data analysis, not feedback memory hidden inside the autonomous source. The intervention requires physical memory access, a clock and a calibrated projector. Those are additional admitted operations; passive archives alone cannot supply them. The separation has a simple controlled tolerance. If each nominated conditional memory state has trace-distance error at most dS and the actual probe effect has operator-norm error at most dP , put d = dS + dP . The parent conditional click probability is at most d and the new one is at least 800/30603 −d. Their admitted intervals are disjoint whenever d < 400/30603 ≃0.01307. This follows from contraction of effect probabilities under trace distance and ∥∆P∥op; it does not infer those calibration premises from passive word equality. The joint-event gap is then at least (800/30603−2d)/3 under the same exact pre-intervention word law. Complete reference/bath equivalence is neither assumed nor inferred from this pointer-level discriminator. The example has one-step record Choi rank eighteen, rather than the minimum nine.
